attribution: Tracy Hunter — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Harbin Ice and Snow World, Heilongjiang
alt: Ice towers, arches and a staircase built from ice blocks at Harbin Ice and Snow Festival in daylight
caption: Towers and arches built from ice blocks at the Harbin Ice and Snow Festival, photographed in daylight. The park is rebuilt each December from blocks cut on the Songhua River and usually closes in late February when the ice softens, which shapes the whole timing of this trip.

commonsFile: File:2011 Harbin Sun Island International Snow Sculpture EXPO 13.JPG
attribution: Caliva — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Large snow sculpture at the Sun Island International Snow Sculpture Expo
caption: Monumental snow sculpture on Sun Island, across the Songhua River from central Harbin. The Expo is the daytime counterpart to the evening ice park and works best in cold, dry snow.

attribution: SmallSonMarex — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Saint Sophia Cathedral, Daoli district, Harbin
alt: Russian-style Saint Sophia Cathedral with green dome in winter, Harbin
caption: The Byzantine-style Saint Sophia Cathedral, built by Russians in the early twentieth century and now an architecture museum. It is the clearest trace of the Russian railway city that Harbin once was.

commonsFile: File:201906 Harbin Central Street at night 08.jpg
attribution: Jonashtand — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Central Street in Harbin at night with European-style facades and pedestrians
caption: Central Street, a pedestrian boulevard of Baroque and Art Nouveau facades from the Russian and early Republican era, photographed here at night in June. In winter the same street carries ice sculptures and food stalls.

attribution: SmallSonMarex — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Siberian tigers in a snowy enclosure at the Siberian Tiger Park in Harbin
caption: Siberian tigers in snow at the Harbin Siberian Tiger Park, a captive-breeding centre for the Amur tiger that visitors tour by caged bus. Tigers are most active in the cold, but the park's feeding shows are a point for the group to judge on ethics.

commonsFile: File:吉林雾凇 Frosty Pines in Jilin - panoramio.jpg
attribution: Jacky Lee — CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Trees along the Songhua River in Jilin City thickly coated with white rime ice
caption: Wusong, or rime ice, coating every branch along the Songhua River in Jilin City. It forms only on the coldest mornings, when warm river water releases vapour that freezes onto the trees.

commonsFile: File:Rime Island Hantun Village 16 Frozen Pear (Dongli) and persimmon.jpg
attribution: 闫恩铭 / Enming Yan — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Hantun Village, Rime Island (Wusong Island), Wulajie, Jilin
alt: Frozen pears and persimmons hanging as winter food in Hantun village near Rime Island
caption: Frozen pears (dongli) and persimmons displayed in Hantun village, a Manchu farming community near Rime Island. Staying in the village rather than only the viewpoint is how the trip meets local life.

attribution: 闫恩铭 / Enming Yan — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Ice sculpture display on Rime Island near Jilin City
caption: Ice sculptures displayed at Rime Island on the Songhua River, a ferry ride from the village of Hantun. The island is the best-known place to see rime ice at dawn between late December and late February.

attribution: ChiralJon — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The frozen Songhua River with snow-covered ice and walkers
caption: The Songhua River frozen solid, thick enough to cut ice for Harbin's festivals and to cross on foot. The river links Harbin and Jilin, the two ends of the rime-ice story.

attribution: Chen Wu — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: China Snow Town (Xuexiang), Shuangfeng Forest Farm, Heilongjiang
alt: Snow-covered wooden houses with glowing roofs in China Snow Town in the morning
caption: China Snow Town at morning, where roofs carry about a metre of snow for months. Cabins with heated kang beds make it a two-night stop for remote forest-farm winter life.

attribution: NASA — Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Changbai Mountain (Paektu), Tianchi crater lake, Jilin
alt: Aerial view of snow-covered Changbai Mountain with the frozen Tianchi crater lake in the centre
caption: Tianchi crater lake frozen and snow-covered inside the rim of Changbai Mountain, in an astronaut photograph taken from orbit. It shows the winter state of the lake the group would see from the north-slope summit road, weather permitting; the lake is shared with North Korea, where it is called Paektu.

attribution: EditQ — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Yanji, Yanbian Korean Autonomous Prefecture, Jilin
alt: View over Yanji city, centre of the Yanbian Korean Autonomous Prefecture
caption: Yanji, capital of the Yanbian Korean Autonomous Prefecture, with bilingual Chinese-Korean signs and a strong Korean food culture of cold noodles, barbecue and rice cakes. It is the base for Changbai Mountain.
